Please read the following multiple-choice questions and provide the most likely correct answer based on the options given.

Context: None

Question: Which of the following is a true statement?

Options: 
A. An experiment is always more reliable than an observational study, regardless of design.
B. Cause-and-effect relationships can only be established through controlled experiments.
C. Increasing the sample size in an observational study can completely eliminate bias.
D. If properly designed, observational studies can establish cause-and-effect relationships just as strongly as properly designed experiments.
E. While properly designed experiments can strongly suggest cause-and-effect relationships, a complete census is the only way of establishing such a relationship.
F. Controlled experiments are often undertaken later to establish cause-and-effect relationships first suggested by observational studies.
G. A census is the least accurate method of establishing cause-and-effect relationships.
H. The sample size of an observational study has no impact on the potential bias.
I. Observational studies can never suggest cause-and-effect relationships.
J. A useful approach to overcome bias in observational studies is to increase the sample size.

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.
